title: Full-series coefficient projection preserving every earlier block
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth affine finite-type scheme over a characteristic-zero field $k$, with etale coordinates $w$, $a\in C$, and $R=\mathcal O(C)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Consider $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in R[[T]]$ in finitely many variables $T$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s\in\mathbf N^n$ be the ordered minimal vertices of a monotone orthant diagram in variables $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$; form degree blocks, final-segment essential variable sets $T^h$, last indices $s_h$, and first-vertex quotient sets $\Delta_i^h$ by deleting nonessential coordinates [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Fix a block $\ell$ with $T=T^\ell$ and a finite $Q$, and suppose that the remaining variables $Z\setminus T^\ell$ are among the coordinates $w$, in their order. The centered Taylor series at $a$ of each $f_i$ has first coefficient $1$ and first exponent $\alpha_i$, read in the Taylor variables $(W,T)$ in total-degree lexicographic order with $W$ before $T$; for $i\le s_\ell$ this exponent is $(0,\alpha_i)$. For $h<\ell$, an earlier test is that the coefficient of $(T^h)^\eta$ is identically zero as a full series in the other variables whenever $\eta$ lies in that prefix diagram and $|\eta|\le Q$. Suppose $P^-$ projects onto their common kernel, is linear over $R[[T\setminus T^{\ell-1}]]$, fixes every $f_i$ with $i>s_{\ell-1}$, and $P^--1$ takes values in $(f_1,\ldots,f_{s_{\ell-1}})$. At $a$ it preserves the first exponent whenever the first monomial passes the earlier tests. Its defining coefficient extractions and full correction columns have regular coefficients on $C$.
Let $D_h$ be the diagram of the first $h$ blocks restricted to $T^h$ and set
$$E=\{\gamma\in D_\ell\setminus(D_{\ell-1}\times\mathbf N^{|T\setminus T^{\ell-1}|}):|\gamma|\le Q\}.$$
Use the actual coordinate order in this product. Each $\gamma\in E$ has a unique assigned pair $(j,\beta)$ with $s_{\ell-1}<j\le s_\ell$, $\beta\in\Delta_j^\ell$, and $\gamma=\alpha_j+\beta$. Put $C_\gamma=P^-(T^\beta f_j)$ and $B_{\eta\gamma}=[T^\eta]C_\gamma\in R$. Then every full $C_\gamma$ passes the earlier tests, differs from $T^\beta f_j$ by an earlier-generator combination, and at $a$ has first exponent $(0,\gamma)$. The matrix $B(a)$ is triangular with diagonal $1$. On the single open $\det B\ne0$, define $v(H)=([T^\eta]H)_{\eta\in E}$ and
$$P_\ell H=P^-H-\sum_{\gamma\in E}(B^{-1}v(P^-H))_\gamma C_\gamma.$$
This is an $R$-linear projection onto the common kernel of every earlier test and all degree-$\le Q$ forbidden coefficient tests for $D_\ell$. It fixes that kernel, has regular coefficients on this one open, and $P_\ell-1$ takes values in $(f_1,\ldots,f_{s_\ell})$. At $a$ it preserves the first exponent of any series whose first monomial passes all these tests. Replacing only $f_i$ with $i>s_\ell$ by $P_\ell f_i$ preserves the generated ideal at every point, every vertex exponent at $a$, and all earlier derivative equations and Jacobians. No tail of a correction column is truncated. If $E$ is empty the sum is zero. All assertions include residue-field extension [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Order $E$ increasingly. By [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division], assigning an exponent to the first vertex dividing it gives disjoint sets $\alpha_j+\Delta_j^\ell$. If $\gamma\in E$, no old vertex divides it, whereas a vertex in the new block does; thus the assigned $j$ is in the claimed range and $\beta=\gamma-\alpha_j$ is unique. Nested essential sets embed every earlier prefix diagram into the old prefix diagram in $T$ (with free complementary coordinates, in their actual order). Hence the monomial $T^\gamma$ passes every earlier test, including those with bound $Q$.

source.place: Agent refinement of BM 1997 Lemma 9.12, (9.13) and Definition 9.14, pp.280--281, on the ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 route; full projected correction columns and simultaneous old tests.

proof.text: Put $G_\gamma=T^\beta f_j$. Multiplying its Taylor expansion by the monomial shifts its first exponent to $(0,\gamma)$ and retains coefficient $1$, by additivity of degree-lex order. Thus $C_\gamma=P^-G_\gamma$ passes every old test and has this first exponent, by the hypotheses on $P^-$; its difference from $G_\gamma$ lies in the earlier-generator ideal. Its first coefficient is also $1$: write $r=[T^\gamma]C_\gamma\in R$. The monomial $rT^\gamma$ lies in the old kernel and is fixed by $P^-$. If $r(a)\ne1$, then $G_\gamma-rT^\gamma$ has first exponent $(0,\gamma)$, whereas its image $C_\gamma-rT^\gamma$ has no term at or below that exponent, contradicting the assumed exponent preservation. This argument uses the actual regular function $r$, so needs no lift of an arbitrary residue-field element.

source.place: Agent refinement of BM 1997 Lemma 9.12, (9.13) and Definition 9.14, pp.280--281, on the ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 route; full projected correction columns and simultaneous old tests.

proof.text: At $a$, the coefficient $B_{\eta\gamma}(a)$ vanishes for $\eta<\gamma$ and equals $1$ for $\eta=\gamma$. In the permutation formula for the determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], every nonidentity permutation has a chosen row smaller than its column, so its product is zero. Therefore $\det B(a)=1$. On $U=D(\det B)$ use $B^{-1}=(\det B)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(B)$; [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] gives both inverse identities. Its entries are regular on $U$, as are all coefficients of the full $C_\gamma$ by the stipulated regular construction of $P^-$. We now use $R$ for the restricted coefficient ring.

source.place: Agent refinement of BM 1997 Lemma 9.12, (9.13) and Definition 9.14, pp.280--281, on the ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 route; full projected correction columns and simultaneous old tests.

proof.text: For $G=P^-H$ and $c=B^{-1}v(G)$, every column belongs to the old kernel; $R$-linearity of the old coefficient tests puts $G-\sum c_\gamma C_\gamma$ in that kernel. Its $E$-coefficient vector is $v(G)-Bc=0$. Every exponent of $D_\ell$ of total degree at most $Q$ either belongs to $E$ or has its old-variable restriction in $D_{\ell-1}$ of degree at most $Q$, so these are exactly all the required new tests together with the old ones. Conversely an $H$ in this common kernel has $P^-H=H$ and $v(H)=0$, giving $P_\ell H=H$. This proves linearity, the asserted image and idempotence.

source.place: Agent refinement of BM 1997 Lemma 9.12, (9.13) and Definition 9.14, pp.280--281, on the ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 route; full projected correction columns and simultaneous old tests.

proof.text:
For every $H$, write $C_\gamma=T^\beta f_j+e_\gamma$ with $e_\gamma$ in the old-generator ideal, as proved in step 2. Then
$$P_\ell H-H=(P^--1)H-\sum_{\gamma\in E}c_\gamma(T^\beta f_j+e_\gamma)\in(f_1,\ldots,f_{s_\ell}).$$
The expression uses the full $e_\gamma$ and full $f_j$; no tail is discarded. All the maps have regular coefficients on $U$, by step 3.

source.place: Agent refinement of BM 1997 Lemma 9.12, (9.13) and Definition 9.14, pp.280--281, on the ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 route; full projected correction columns and simultaneous old tests.

proof.text: Let the nonzero Taylor series of $H$ at $a$ have first exponent $\mu$, and suppose its first monomial passes every test. Then $G=P^-H$ has first exponent $\mu$. Put $L=\kappa(a)$. Since every full $C_\gamma$ begins at $(0,\gamma)$, its Taylor coefficient matrix $\widehat B$ satisfies the support inequalities of [lem-trf-shift-filtered-matrix-inverse] with weights $u_\gamma=\gamma$; its constant determinant is $1$ by step 3. Apply that lemma to $\widehat B^{-1}$. Every term $W^\delta T^\eta$ contributing to $v(G)$ has exponent strictly greater than $\mu$: it cannot be smaller, and equality is excluded because the leading monomial passes the new tests. The inverse support inequality implies that every term $W^\epsilon$ of $c_\gamma$ satisfies $(\epsilon,\gamma)>\mu$: multiply a term of $(\widehat B^{-1})_{\gamma\eta}$ by a term of $[T^\eta]G$ and add their inequalities. Multiplication by $C_\gamma$, whose terms have exponents at least $(0,\gamma)$, keeps this strict inequality. Thus the entire correction has no term at or below $\mu$, and $P_\ell H$ retains the first term of $G$, in particular its first exponent.

source.place: Agent refinement of BM 1997 Lemma 9.12, (9.13) and Definition 9.14, pp.280--281, on the ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 route; full projected correction columns and simultaneous old tests.

proof.text: For $i>s_\ell$, minimality of the full vertex $\alpha_i$ means that no earlier vertex divides it. Its monomial therefore passes each prefix test, even when some of its coordinates lie among $W$. Step 6 retains its vertex exponent. Keep $f_i$ unchanged for $i\le s_\ell$ and replace the others by $f'_i=P_\ell f_i$. Step 5 writes each $f'_i-f_i$ using only the unchanged prefix generators; the two inclusions of generated ideals follow by solving this same equality for $f_i$. Specializing at any point of $U$ gives the same ideal equality in its Taylor ring. All earlier derivative equations and their Jacobians involve prefix generators with index at most $s_\ell$; these generators, the coordinates and their derivative operators are unchanged, so those equations and matrices are identical.

source.place: Agent refinement of BM 1997 Lemma 9.12, (9.13) and Definition 9.14, pp.280--281, on the ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 route; full projected correction columns and simultaneous old tests.

proof.text: For $E=\varnothing$, the determinant is the empty determinant $1$, $v$ is empty and $P_\ell=P^-$; the old tests already include every required coefficient. All preceding calculations are coefficientwise finite sums and products and multiplication by $\det B^{-1}$; after any residue-field extension they are the same identities. The initial coefficients equal to $1$ remain $1$, so the same leading-exponent and ideal conclusions hold. This also covers the first block (empty old prefix), no transverse variables, and $Q$ below the degree of the current block.
